title: On sigma0 26.5, seven CMIP6 models change water age as much as observed but change oxygen less, as AOU per year of age is low; model tests support the ventilation cause (1980-2014)
abstract: Question: on the sigma0 = 26.5 density surface, do CMIP6 models reproduce the observed decadal oxygen (O2), AOU and water-age changes at BATS, CalCOFI and GLODAP repeat lines, and does the observational tracer test of ventilation work when the truth is known? Approach: we streamed historical output (1980-2014, one member each) of seven models with O2 and ideal age, three with CFC/SF6 and two with remineralization, put it on density surfaces, sampled it at the same line tracks and boxes, and applied the tests of the prior studies. Results: on North Atlantic lines, model AOU per year of age was 0.19-0.95 times the observed 5.2 umol/kg/yr (median 0.39); in the North Pacific 0.09-0.93 times. Observed age changes exceeded the model 95th percentile on 0-3 of 7 lines, but observed O2 changes on 4-6 of 7 lines (1-5 with conservative observed intervals). At CalCOFI the observed variability of 10-yr O2 changes was 1.4-5.7 times the model values. With model ideal age, the observational test gave 12-15 of 16 same-sign pairs (observed 13) and slopes of 0.15-0.48 on the AOU/age prediction (observed 0.55); thus a slope below 1 does not show a respiration decrease. In IPSL-CM6A-LR, AOU and age rose on 9 of 9 lines while remineralization fell on 9 of 9; MPI-ESM-1-2-HAM was similar. CFC TTD age changes had the sign of ideal-age changes in 88-94% of North Atlantic pairs, but slopes of 0.56-1.78, and failed in old North Pacific water. Limitations: one member per model; observed noise is larger than model-mean noise; observed TTD ages and model ideal ages differ; a x1e6 correction of the UKESM1 CFC-11 field; MPI-HAM remineralization used only in relative terms.

citations.reason: We use its repeat-line tracks, bins and pair results, and apply its test to models; models support its sign-based ventilation conclusion and show that its AOU/age slope is biased low.
